content.value_statement: Expo Router API routes can be confusing when secrets, deployment, and runtime limits are involved. This skill gives practical patterns for building, testing, and deploying routes on EAS Hosting.
actual_capabilities: Explains when Expo API routes are useful and when another backend option fits better.
Shows file naming for static and dynamic Expo Router API routes.
Demonstrates GET, POST, PUT, and DELETE handler patterns with Request and Response.
Covers server-side environment variables for API keys and database clients.
Describes local testing, EAS deployment, and Cloudflare Workers runtime limits.
Includes examples for CORS, authentication helpers, external API proxies, and client calls.
limitations: Does not create a complete backend architecture by itself.
Does not automatically verify production security settings.
Examples use placeholders and must be adapted to each project.
Focuses on Expo Router and EAS Hosting, not generic Node servers.

use_cases.title: Add Server Logic to an Expo App
use_cases.description: Create API routes for validation, data access, and mobile app features that need server execution.

use_cases.title: Protect Third-Party API Keys
use_cases.description: Move OpenAI, Stripe, weather, or database keys into server-side route handlers instead of client code.

use_cases.title: Prepare Routes for EAS Hosting
use_cases.description: Check local testing commands, deployment steps, and Cloudflare Workers limits before shipping.

prompt_templates.title: Create a First Route
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a simple API endpoint.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to design a basic Expo Router API route for my app. Include the route file path, supported method, response shape, and local test steps.

prompt_templates.title: Handle Request Data
prompt_templates.scenario: Build a route that reads query parameters, headers, or a request body.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to plan an Expo API route that accepts request data. Explain validation, error responses, and which HTTP status codes to use.

prompt_templates.title: Proxy a Secret API
prompt_templates.scenario: Protect a service key behind a server-side endpoint.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to design an Expo API route that calls a third-party service with a server-side secret. Include environment variable setup and client call guidance.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Production Route Set
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced audit before deployment to EAS Hosting.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to review my Expo API route plan for EAS Hosting. Check route structure, authentication, CORS, runtime limits, deployment steps, and missing safeguards.

output_examples.input: A developer asks where to put a new users endpoint in an Expo Router project.
output_examples.output: The response identifies the route file location, supported URL path, needed methods, validation steps, and a local testing command.

output_examples.input: A team wants to hide a weather service key from a React Native screen.
output_examples.output: The response recommends a server-side proxy route, an environment variable name, client request behavior, and safe error handling.

output_examples.input: A release owner asks whether API routes are ready for EAS Hosting.
output_examples.output: The response checks deployment prerequisites, runtime limits, secret storage, unsupported Node APIs, and route testing coverage.

best_practices: Keep secrets in server environment variables and never in client code.
Validate and sanitize request data before database writes or external API calls.
Test routes locally before deploying them to EAS Hosting.
anti_patterns: Using API routes for public static data that needs no server logic.
Putting API keys or database credentials inside React Native components.
Assuming Node filesystem or native modules are available on EAS Hosting.

faq.question: What does this skill help me build?
faq.answer: It helps you plan and implement Expo Router API routes for server-side logic, proxies, validation, and deployment.

faq.question: Does it support EAS Hosting?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes deployment steps and notes about the Cloudflare Workers runtime used by EAS Hosting.

faq.question: Can it help protect API keys?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains how to keep keys in server environment variables and call external services from API routes.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill is packaged for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.

faq.question: Does it replace backend security review?
faq.answer: No. It provides route patterns, but production authentication, CORS, rate limits, and validation still need review.

faq.question: What projects fit this skill best?
faq.answer: It fits Expo Router apps that need lightweight server endpoints hosted with EAS Hosting.
